_comment: StyleProfile — per-style construction knobs for Structure Generation v2. Thickness/ceiling values in CUBES (1 cube = 1 m); roof 'pitch_deg' in DEGREES. GROUNDED per the medieval period (see docs/StructureGenerationV2.md). Each style carries a primary `source` + a per-value `sources` map (the grounding rule). Confidence is noted inline: sourced vs INFERRED (from a sourced system, low confidence). Material gaps (thatch, clay tile) are placeholders pending MaterialTextureNeeds.md. NOTE: the realizer must be wired to honor roof.pitch_deg (currently hardcoded) — follow-up.

timber_cottage.description: Humble medieval timber frame + wattle-and-daub, thatch roof, on a low stone plinth.
timber_cottage.source: medieval timber-frame vernacular (wattle & daub on close studs, stone plinth + sill beam, thatch)

sources.interior_wall: INFERRED ~0.10-0.15 m: light daub/timber screen, thinner than exterior
sources.foundation_wall: 14th-c half-timbered building on 'narrow sleeper walls 18 inches' = 0.46 m -> 0.444 (4 micro) (medievalists.net)
sources.roof.pitch_deg: thatch demands >=45 deg, usually 50 deg, to shed water (roofonline.com; English Heritage Buildings)
sources.roof.material: PLACEHOLDER: real roof is THATCH; engine lacks a thatch material (MaterialTextureNeeds.md)
sources.ceiling_target: ANTHROPOMETRIC (not period): character clearance (character_design_constraints.json) + IRC R305 7 ft floor

stone_manor.description: Medieval stone hall / manor: thick rubble-cored ashlar walls, tiled roof, tall hall.
stone_manor.source: medieval stone manor / hall house (2-3 ft walls, two faces + rubble core, clay-tile roof)

sources.exterior_wall: stone manor/hall wall 0.6-0.9 m (2-3 ft), two faces + rubble core (castlesandmanorhouses.com; Wikipedia Hall house)
sources.roof.material: PLACEHOLDER: real roof is CLAY TILE/slate; engine lacks the material (MaterialTextureNeeds.md)
sources.ceiling_target: ANTHROPOMETRIC + status: grand halls 'higher than wide' (Wikipedia Great hall) + character clearance
